paragraphs.text: Cornelia de Lange syndrome-4 (CDLS4) is a cohesinopathy caused by mutation in the cohesin gene RAD21. Affected individuals have growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlap those of classic Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS), but cognitive impairment is generally milder than in CdLS caused by mutation in other cohesin genes (Deardorff et al., 2012; Krab et al., 2020). Some patients with heterozygous RAD21 variants have holoprosencephaly (Kruszka et al., 2019; Krab et al., 2020).

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations, 24 of whom were previously unpublished. In the 29 individuals with full clinical information (cohort A), the phenotype was an attenuated form of CdLS compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, particularly with regard to facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition, and behavior. Features in cohort A included postnatal microcephaly in 16 of 28, postnatal short stature in 10 of 27, synophrys in 19 of 28, long and/or smooth philtrum in 26 of 29, short fifth finger in 23 of 28, cleft palate in 6 of 25, heart anomalies in 9 of 23, hearing loss in 8 of 24, and gastroesophageal reflux in 13 of 25; no major limb malformations were found (0 of 29). Short stature and microcephaly typically developed postnatally. Unusual anomalies included vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and relatively frequent malformations of foregut-derived structures.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous RAD21 mutations in CDLS4 occur de novo or are inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. Minor et al. (2014) found that a RAD21 in-frame deletion was inherited from the patient's mother, and discussed variable clinical presentation within families and low penetrance of the mutations. Boyle et al. (2017) found a RAD21 variant in a patient with mild CdLS and in the patient's mother and 2 aunts, none of whom fulfilled diagnostic criteria for CdLS; they suggested that RAD21 variants are associated with incomplete penetrance and that such individuals may be underdiagnosed. Krab et al. (2020) found that variants were familial in 9 of 21 index cases in whom inheritance could be established.
